lines.code: int testarray[N]; /* elements from ar[0] to ar[N-1]; */

lines.explanation: Here we call function readarray that will read N numbers from the user and place them into the array passed as the first parameter. Since it is passed by value, we will see changes,

lines.code: printf("Sum = %d, max = %d\n", sumarray(testarray, N), testarray[maxelement(testarray, N)]);
lines.explanation: During the execution of printf, functions sumarray and maxelement will be called.

This function takes an array and an integer as parameters and returns an integer. Note that the integer array ar is passed by reference. Our changes of the array will be visible by the calling function.
This loop will run exactly n_of_elements times
Promt to enter i-th element of the array
The entered number is read and placed into the array element with index i.
As any integer function, readarray should return some integer value. Readarray unconditionally returns 0, but this value is not used by the calling function in this example.
The sum of the array elements is accumulated in local variable sum
By calling return we pass the value of sum to the calling funcion as the result of the function call of sumarray

lines.code: /* finding index of max array element */

lines.explanation: maxind is used to store the position of the running maximum element in the array. We initialize it to 0.
We check every element of the array starting from the second one (ar[1]) againts the stored maximum
If the stored maximum (element ar[maxind]) is less than the current element, the we have to change the maximum to the current element.
